sections.h2: What is Baltimore County, Maryland, and how does it relate to Baltimore City?
sections.html:
Baltimore County is the third most populous county in Maryland, and it partly surrounds the independent city of Baltimore without including it. Towson is the county seat. Baltimore City became independent of the county on July 4, 1851, under the state's 1851 constitution, and Towson was chosen as county seat by referendum on February 13, 1854.

That split matters for sellers because the county offices described here bill and record only for properties on the county side of the line. Baltimore City runs its own tax and land records offices.

The county was founded in 1659 and named for Cecil Calvert, the second Baron Baltimore. It once included the present city plus Cecil and Harford counties. It covers 682 square miles, 598 of them land, and the 2020 census counted 854,535 residents.

sections.h2: What is the geography and what are the main communities in Baltimore County?
sections.html:
Baltimore County runs from the Chesapeake Bay shoreline in the southeast to hills along the Pennsylvania border, where the highest point reaches about 960 feet. It straddles the Piedmont in the northwest and the Atlantic Coastal Plain in the south and southeast, and the northern part is primarily rural.

Dundalk is the largest community, and the county also includes a rural north, so lot size and property type vary widely from one address to the next. The state's assessors value all of them, using the same three-year cycle.

sections.h2: What does the Baltimore County economy look like?
sections.html:
Baltimore County's major sectors are education, government and health care. A Wikipedia employer list names the Social Security Administration and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services at 14,948 jobs, Baltimore County Public Schools at 14,608, county government at 8,429 and MedStar Franklin Square Medical Center at 3,500. Black and Decker is based in Towson.

Higher education adds more local anchors: Towson University, the University of Maryland, Baltimore County in Catonsville, Goucher College, Stevenson University, and Community College of Baltimore County campuses in Catonsville, Essex and Dundalk. Baltimore County Public Schools is the county's only public school district apart from one charter school.

Transit includes the Metro SubwayLink to Owings Mills, the Light RailLink north to Hunt Valley and south through Baltimore Highlands, and MARC stops at Halethorpe, St. Denis and Martin State Airport. The county has been governed under a charter since 1956, with a county executive and a seven-member council.

sections.h2: How were Baltimore County values reassessed for 2026?
sections.html:
Baltimore County was part of the group SDAT reassessed for January 1, 2026, and its full cash value rose 12.1 percent over the three years from January 1, 2023. The notices for that group were mailed on December 30, 2025.

  • Combined value: $47.17 billion to $52.88 billion.
  • Residential value: $34.02 billion to $38.22 billion, up 12.4 percent.
  • Commercial value: $13.16 billion to $14.65 billion, up 11.3 percent.
  • Share of residential properties that increased: 85.93 percent.

Under SDAT's explanation, an increase phases in evenly over three years, while a decrease applies fully in the 2026 tax year. You can appeal within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment, and appeals start with SDAT before moving to the county appeals board and the Maryland Tax Court. SDAT keeps an office at 300 East Joppa Road, Room 602, in Towson.

sections.h2: How and when do you pay Baltimore County property tax?
sections.html:
Baltimore County issues real property tax bills on July 1, and owner-occupied homes can pay in two installments, with the first payable through September 30 and the second payable through December 31. The county's payment schedule lists July 1 and December 1 as the dates each installment is due, with September 30 and December 31 as the last days to pay without penalty or interest.

Semiannual billing is for owner-occupied residential property and small businesses, and the owner must occupy the residence for more than six months of a 12-month period. Each installment covers half of the state and county tax, half of the homestead and homeowners' credits, and half of any metropolitan charges. If a mortgage escrow pays the first installment, no December bill is issued, but the owner still has to make sure the second payment is made on time. To stay an annual payer, notify the mortgage company 60 days before the tax year.

The Office of Budget and Finance is at 400 Washington Avenue, Room 150, Towson, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call 410-887-2404 or email financeinfo@baltimorecountymd.gov.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid Baltimore County tax bill?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill in Baltimore County can lead to the property being sold at the annual June tax sale, and the county mails its notices on a fixed calendar. A missed first installment makes the account delinquent, and balances unpaid after December 31 are also delinquent.

  • February: delinquent notices are mailed, and partial payments are accepted until the end of the month.
  • End of February: deadline to apply for the Hardship Installment Payment Program to avoid a sale.
  • March 1: a Final Tax Sale notice gives 30 days to pay.
  • Around May 1: properties scheduled for sale are posted on the county website.
  • June: the annual tax sale takes place.

The county says an owner has six months from the sale date to redeem. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman describes redemption as available until a court forecloses the right, and says Baltimore County's older notices cite 12 percent per year. Because those two descriptions differ, ask the county and a lawyer which one controls your case. Partial payments do not stop interest, though they usually reduce what accrues.

sections.h2: What should a Baltimore County seller know about lien certificates?
sections.html:
A lien certificate shows the status of unpaid taxes or charges on a property account, and Baltimore County requires one before any real property transfer. The certificate costs $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application, and in most cases all unpaid taxes and charges must be paid before a transfer.

Ask for it early. The Transfer Tax Section at 410-887-2416 answers account-specific lien questions, and the Liens Section of the Clerk of the Court at 410-887-2622 handles legal liens that show on credit reports. Our Baltimore County land records guide covers the recording side of the same sale.

sections.h2: Does Baltimore County regulate rental properties before a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, every rental property in Baltimore County needs a rental license or an exemption license under County Code Section 35-5-201, and an owner must be licensed before a tenant moves in. That covers dwellings with six or fewer units, including short-term rentals, and dwellings with seven or more units.

  • Licenses last three years and can be renewed for further three-year terms.
  • Short-term rental licenses cost $300 per unit.
  • For seven or more units, an owner with fewer than three code violations in three years may use a self-certification affidavit; otherwise 10 percent of units are inspected.
  • Within one mile of Towson University's main campus, licenses may be restricted where the rental rate is 30 percent or more.

Rental Housing Registration is at 111 West Chesapeake Avenue, Room 216, Towson, at 410-887-6060. A landlord selling a tenant-occupied house should check whether the license is current before listing.

faqs.q: When are Baltimore County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are issued July 1, and the first installment of a semiannual bill is payable through September 30. The second installment is payable through December 31 to avoid penalty or interest.

faqs.q: Who can pay Baltimore County property tax in two installments?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied residential property and small businesses qualify. The owner must live in the home for more than six months of a 12-month period.

faqs.q: How much is a Baltimore County lien certificate?
faqs.a: The fee is $55, payable to Baltimore County, Maryland, with a completed application. The county says one is required before any real property transfer.

faqs.q: When is the Baltimore County tax sale?
faqs.a: The annual tax sale is held in June. The county mails a Final Tax Sale notice on March 1 and posts properties on its website around May 1.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Baltimore County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the Notice of Assessment to appeal to SDAT. The appeal path then continues to the county appeals board and the Maryland Tax Court.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a Baltimore County rental house?
faqs.a: A license is required to rent the property in the first place, so a landlord should confirm it is current before listing. Call Rental Housing Registration at 410-887-6060 with questions.
